newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Oil output at Australia's Bass Strait rises - Esso.
newsitem.headline: Oil output at Australia's Bass Strait rises - Esso.

text.p: Exxon Corp unit Esso Australia Ltd said on Monday that oil production from Australia's Bass Strait, which has been in decline since 1985, has increased recently by about 35,000 barrels per day (bpd) to around 235,000 bpd.

The increase is a result of the installation of two new offshore platforms which at full capacity will produce about 25,000 bpd on a combined basis, Nick Heath, a director of Esso, told the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association conference.
"Those platforms will peak in production later this year," he said.
The two platforms, the West Tuna and Bream B, were commissioned in late 1996.
The Bass Strait offshore oil project is a 50-50 joint venture between Esso and BHP Petroleum, a unit of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd. Esso is the operator.
The Bass Strait field's output peaked in 1985 when it produced at an average rate of about 500,000 bpd.
